title: Language Access in Palliative Care: What the Data Shows
summary: Learn what research shows about palliative care language access, goals-of-care communication, symptom management, hospice enrollment.
body_markdown:
###


They can affect symptom assessment, understanding of prognosis, goals-of-care discussions, advance care planning, hospice conversations, and follow-up with patients and families.


###


Goals-of-care discussions include prognosis, uncertainty, values, and treatment tradeoffs. Language support is needed for the reasoning behind the decision, not only the final choice.


###


Some observational studies have found differences in palliative care use, advance care planning, hospital use, and place of death. These studies show disparities but do not prove that language alone causes them.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation can support serious-illness care when the system is built for clinical communication and the care team confirms understanding and knows how to respond to unclear interpretation.


###


Use professional language support early, explain hospice in plain language, provide multilingual written materials, let families participate without requiring them to interpret, and carry language preferences across home visits and follow-up.
